findings.text: _judge_head_move reads node.get("done_when") straight off the pointer record, but the reviewed change moved that field into <run dir>/node.json: list_live returns the slim node and the merge at recovery_review_dispatch.py:4148 ({**lifecycle, **record}) lets the caller's slim node override read_pointer's hydrated one, so the review-need judge sees an empty done-when for every run composed through the sweep; re_review_prediction at :1895 reads it the same way. Both belong on runs.node_field(record, "done_when").

data = node_definition(record) always returns a dict, so the following `if not isinstance(data, Mapping): raise CrewError(... records no node definition)` can no longer fire; a pointer carrying no node now rebuilds an all-empty TaskNode instead of raising the refusal; the guard should test the mapping it read before hydrating, or node_definition should report an absent node.

assert rebuilt.as_dict() == at_base.as_dict() compares two nodes that both resolve through runs.node_definition, and the "inline" arm at :235-:238 is itself built with that accessor, so the pair moves together and cannot redden on a hydration defect; the fixture-anchored asserts at :246-:248 are what guard it. inline.pop("node_body") at :238 also pops a record-level key that is never set, leaving the node-level node_body in the inline arm.
